newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Monde ordered to pay France's Lagardere damages.
newsitem.headline: Le Monde ordered to pay France's Lagardere damages.

text.p: The French daily Le Monde was ordered on Wednesday to pay industrialist Jean-Luc Lagardere 200,000 francs ($36,000) in damages for publishing erroneous information about him.
Lagardere had sought 1.5 million francs in libel damages over the November article which said he had been placed under judicial investigation for "misuse of corporate funds, fraud and forgery".

In fact he has been placed under investigation only for "misuse of corporate funds" in a case concerning methods of payment to executives of Lagardere Groupe, which controls missile-maker Matra and multimedia/publishing firm Hachette.
Under French law, being placed under investigation is a first step to a possible prosecution but does not automatically lead to trial.

The court said Le Monde had failed to exercise due caution in publishing information "from insufficiently checked sources". It ordered the afternoon daily to publish the judgment on its front page and in three other newspapers.
In its defence, Le Monde said its erroneous information came from a magistrate in the Paris public prosecutor's office.
